items.title: Mannréttindaskrifstofa einnig lögð niður
items.summary: The Reykjavík City Human Rights Office has been shut down following a city council decision, leading to layoffs and reassignments. Mayor Hildur Björnsdóttir had advocated for the closure, citing the office's annual cost of hundreds of millions and Reykjavík being the only municipality to operate such an office.

items.title: Tekist á um nýtt fyrirkomulag á fyrsta fundi
items.summary: The Reykjavík city council's new preschool and daycare board held a contentious first meeting. Employee and management representatives criticized the majority's proposal to discuss abolishing the single teaching license and shortening preschool teacher education, as well as the restructuring of the education boards. The debate centers on the importance of preschool education, teacher qualifications, and the administrative framework for schools in the city.

items.title: Þrjú útköll í einu: Ofkældist á Fimmvörðuhálsi
items.summary: Rescue teams responded to three separate incidents in the Icelandic highlands. One involved a hiker suffering from hypothermia on Fimmvörðuháls, while others were wet and cold. Another call-out concerned a tourist in Kerlingarfjöll, and a third involved a couple whose car got stuck north of Sultartangarlón.

items.title: Einfalda og nútímavæða byggingarreglugerð
items.summary: The Housing and Construction Authority (HMS) has introduced proposed changes to Iceland's building regulations. The aim is to simplify the complex and outdated rules, making the construction industry more efficient and competitive without compromising quality. Key changes include reducing the length of regulatory chapters, lessening oversight for simple private structures, and implementing a digital building permit application process standardized across all municipalities.

items.title: Tilkynnt um uppsagnirnar fyrir fram
items.summary: Reykjavík City has announced layoffs and organizational changes, including the closure of the Office of Communications and Events, the Human Rights Office, and the Mayor's Office Policy and Development Team. These measures are attributed to cost-cutting and restructuring efforts, with several employees losing their jobs or being reassigned.

items.title: Umfangsmiklar breytingar: 18 störf lögð niður
items.summary: Reykjavík City is implementing extensive administrative changes, including the elimination of 18 jobs and the restructuring of several offices like human rights and communications. These measures aim to save 280-330 million ISK annually, as the city's mayor stated current operations are financially unsustainable for statutory services. The changes, approved by the city council, also involve tightening financial controls and reducing employee travel.

items.title: Ráða í sex til sjö ný störf
items.summary: Reykjavík City is undergoing administrative restructuring, which includes eliminating 18 positions and moving 9 others, primarily within the Mayor's and City Secretary's offices. Despite the layoffs, 6-7 new positions will be created as part of the changes. These measures are projected to save the city 280-330 million ISK annually in operating costs.
items.spin_note: The headline highlights new hires but omits the context of 18 positions being eliminated as part of the same restructuring.

items.title: Niðurrif í fullum gangi á hluta Flataskóla í Garðabæ
items.summary: Demolition is underway on older sections of Flataskóli school in Garðabær, a project managed by H2Orka and overseen by VSB Verkfræðistofa. Approximately 1,170 square meters of concrete school buildings, built between 1958 and 1993, are being removed. This demolition is part of a larger redevelopment and renewal plan for the school area, with completion anticipated by mid-August 2026.

items.title: Opnun Hornafjarðarfljótabrúar langþráð en há veggjöld komi á óvart
items.summary: The Hornafjarðarfljót bridge and a new road have opened, shortening the Ring Road by 12 km and improving connectivity for the local community. While the opening was long-awaited, the mayor of Hornafjörður expressed surprise and concern over the high toll fees, questioning if less populated areas are being charged more than populous ones.

items.title: Jökulfell ehf. með eina tilboðið í vetrarþjónustu á Suðausturlandi
items.summary: The Icelandic Road and Coastal Administration received only one bid for a three-year winter service contract on a key route in Southeast Iceland. The bid from Jökulfell ehf. was 233.2 million ISK, which is 25.1% higher than the estimated cost. The agency is now reviewing the offer for snow removal and anti-icing services.

items.title: Synjaði umdeildu deiluskipulagi á Suðurlandsbraut
items.summary: The new city council majority in Reykjavík has rejected a controversial zoning plan for Suðurlandsbraut, citing concerns that it would restrict local businesses and is based on outdated transportation assumptions. This decision, which delays the first phase of the Borgarlína public transport project, was met with opposition from the Social Democratic Alliance, who argue it jeopardizes crucial infrastructure improvements. The majority intends to re-evaluate the project in light of broader city interests and a revised transport strategy.

items.title: 30.06.2026 Sambyggð 14 í Þorlákshöfn: Viðhald og Endurbætur 2026
items.summary: The homeowners association of Sambyggð 14 in Þorlákshöfn is seeking bids for extensive exterior maintenance and renovations. The project includes tearing down old cladding, pouring new foundations for window systems, constructing pavements, and enlarging balconies. Bids are due by June 30, 2026, with project completion expected by April 8, 2027.

items.title: 20.08.2026 Reykjavíkurborg býður út trjáfellingar og hirðingu grænna svæða
items.summary: Reykjavík City is issuing a tender for a framework agreement covering tree felling and the maintenance of green areas throughout the city. This service, managed by the Environment and Planning Department, includes tasks such as thinning forests, timber extraction, and pruning. The agreement will initially be for one year, with options for three one-year extensions, potentially lasting up to four years.

items.title: 15.07.2026 Grundarfjarðarbær auglýsir starf skipulags- og/eða byggingarfulltrúa
items.summary: Grundarfjarðarbær is advertising for a planning and/or building official. The role involves managing planning and building permits, overseeing construction, and participating in the town's ongoing development, including new infrastructure and community projects. The municipality is seeking professionals with backgrounds in urban planning, architecture, engineering, or related fields.

items.title: 20.08.2026 Jarðvinna boðin út fyrir nýtt öryggisfangelsi á Stóra-Hrauni
items.summary: Framkvæmdasýslan – Ríkiseignir has issued a tender for extensive earthworks for a new 128-bed high-security prison at Stóra-Hraun, replacing the current facility at Litla-Hraun. This significant government project will be built in two phases, with the first phase including general prison wards, a school, workshops, and staff facilities. The tender covers site preparation, utility installation, and other foundational work for this major infrastructure development.

items.title: HMS leggur til einfaldari og nútímalegri byggingarreglugerð
items.summary: The Housing and Construction Authority (HMS) has proposed a new, simplified, and modernized building regulation. The aim is to streamline the building permit process, enhance consumer protection, and reduce construction costs by eliminating unnecessary administrative burdens and introducing risk-based supervision. This initiative is part of a broader government effort to improve efficiency and foster innovation in the Icelandic construction sector.
